 Judgment

This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.
2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:

On 17-07-2022 at about 3.30 p.m., the petitioner was riding his TVS Star City motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-11- EM-2089, from Sagya to Halaguru, Iggaluru main road, very carefully, cautiously, on extreme left side of the road.

When he reached near Iggaluru Canal, near Sagya Village, at that time a the rider of Yamaha motorbike bearing Reg. No.KA- 05-KG-8297, rode the same with high speed, in rash and negligent manner, so as to endanger to human life, without observing traffic rules and regulations and dashed against the motorcycle of the petitioner from behind.
Due to said impact, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries all over the body.
Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to G. Madegowda Super Speciality Hospital, wherein he took treatment as an in-patient.
Earlier to the accident he was working as Supervisor at Garments Company and was earning a sum of Rs.25,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
The Halaguru Police have registered the case against the driver of the said Yamaha motor bike for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 337 of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 12% per annum.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared through their counsel and filed their separate written statements.
4. The respondent No.1 in her written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.

She has admitted that, she is the owner of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-05-KG-8297 and the same is insured with the respondent No.2 vide policy No.3005/237258951/00/000 and it was valid as on the date of accident.
Therefore, this respondent is not liable to pay the compensation as claimed in the petition.

She has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries,
medical expenses and treatment taken by him.
Further she has denied the alleged accident having occurred at the place date and time and a case registered by the police and the involvement of the aforesaid vehicle in the alleged accident.
Further she has contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
For the above denials and contentions, she has prayed to dismiss the petition.

2 5.
Whereas, the respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
It has denied the issuance of insurance policy in favour of respondent No.1 in respect of vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-05- KG-8297.
Further it has denied the involvement of the offending vehicle in the alleged accident.

Further it is contended that, the petition is liable to be dismissed for non- joinder of necessary parties i.e. insurer/insured of the motorcycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-11-EM-2089.
It has contended that, the petition is bad for non compliance of provisions under Section 134(C) of Motor Vehicles Act.

Further it is contended that, this accident has taken place due to the negligence of the petitioner himself, he was not wearing the helmet with ISI mark,
due to the said reason he has sustained injuries to the head and he himself is contributed for causing the injuries.
Further it is contended that, the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-11-EM- 2089 was not having valid and effective driving licence to ride the said motorcycle.
Due to the said reason the accident has taken place.
Hence, entire negligence is on the part of the petitioner himself.

Further it is contended that, the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-05-KG-8297 was not having valid and effective driving licence to drive the specified class of vehicle involved in the alleged accident and the insured has willfully handed over the said vehicle to the driver who was not authorized to drive the offending vehicle, as on the date of accident.
Hence, this respondent is not liable to indemnify the present claim petition, in view of breach of the policy conditions.
It has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries, medical expenses and treatment taken by him.
Further, it has sought permission to contest the matter on all the grounds available under Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
Further it is contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
For the above denials and contentions, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

6. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident alleged to have occurred on 17-07-2022 at about 3.30 p.m., on Halaguru-Rudrakshipura road, near Iggaluru Canal, Sagya Village, Halaguru Hobli,
Malavalli Taluk, Mandya District, due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the Yamaha motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-05-KG-8297 ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation ?

If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3.

What order or Award ?
7.
In order to prove his case, the petitioner has got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 11 documents as Ex.P.1 to 11.

On the other hand, the respondent No.2 has examined Dr. Mourya G.S.,
Orthopedic Surgeon as R.W.1 and its Legal Manager as R.W.2 and got marked 4 documents as Ex.R.1 to 4.
Whereas, the respondent No.1 has not adduced any evidence on her behalf.
8. I have heard the arguments of both the sides and perused the entire material placed on record.

3 9.

My findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1: Affirmative Issue No.2: Partly Affirmative Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:
REASONS 10. Issue No.1: It is specific case of the petitioner that, on 17-07-2022 at about 3.30 p.m., when the petitioner was riding his TVS Star City motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-11- EM-2089, from Sagya to Halaguru, Iggaluru main road, carefully, on extreme left side of the road and reached near Iggaluru Canal, near Sagya Village, at that time the rider of offending Yamaha motorbike bearing Reg.
No.KA-05-KG- 8297, rode the same with high speed, in rash and negligent manner, without observing traffic rules and regulations and dashed against the motorcycle of the petitioner from behind.
Due to said impact, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries all over the body.
Further it is contended that, earlier to the accident he was working as Supervisor at Garments Company and was earning a sum of Rs.25,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
11. In order to prove his case, the petitioner has got examined himself as P.W.1 by filing examination-in-chief affidavit, wherein he has reiterated the entire averments made in the petition.
Further, in support of his oral evidence, the petitioner has got marked total 11 documents as Ex.P.1 to 11.

Out of the said documents, Ex.P.1 is true copy of F.I.R., Ex.P.2 is true copy of first information statement, Ex.P.3 is true copy of Spot mahazer, Ex.P.4 is true copy of Motor Vehicle Accident report,

Ex.P.5 is true copy of Wound certificate, Ex.P.6 is true copy of Charge- sheet, Ex.P.7 is true copy of MLC extract, Ex.P.8 is Discharge summary, Ex.P.9 are Medical bills (total 9), Ex.P.10 are Prescriptions and Ex.P.11 is notarized copy of Aadhar card.
12.

On meticulously going through the police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 7, prima-facia it reveals that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending Yamaha motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-05-KG-8297 and dashing the same to the ongoing motorcycle of the petitioner.
Further it reveals that, in the said accident the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries on his head, right shoulder and right wrist.

The investigation officer in his final report, marked as Ex.P.6, has clearly stated that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending Yamaha motorcycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-05-KG-8297 and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.

13. At the outset, is it pertinent to note that, in the present case, the date, time and place of accident,
issuance of insurance policy by the respondent No.2 in respect of Yamaha motorcycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-05-KG-8297 and its validity as on the date of accident, are not in dispute.

The respondent No.1 & 2 have specifically denied the above averred facts and circumstances of the accident and they have taken specific defence that, the alleged accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the petitioner/rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-11-EM- 2089 himself, who rode the same with high speed, without holding valid and effective driving licence, without wearing helmet and sustained injuries and the Yamaha motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-05-KG-8297 was not at all Kalappa.

4 involved in the alleged accident.
But, the respondent No.1 has not adduced any evidence to establish the said contentions.
Whereas, the respondent No.2 has examined Dr. Mourya G. S., Orthopaedic Surgeon as R.W.1 and its authorized person/Legal Manager as R.W.2 and got marked 4 documents as Ex.R.1 to 4.
The R.W.1 has produced MLC Register Extract and MLC Intimation with respect to accident in question.
Further he has deposed that, as per Ex.R.1 the accident has taken place in between two wheeler and four wheeler and the said information has been provided by the attendant of the petitioner.
Accordingly, he has sent the intimation to the concerned Police Station.

Further, in the cross-examination he has clearly stated that, as per the initial statement given by the attendants of the patient, the accident has taken place in between two wheeler and a four wheeler vehicles.
Later, the attendants of the patient have again approached the duty doctor and stated that, the said accident has taken place in between 2 two wheeler vehicles.
But, he has clearly admitted the suggestion made to him that, infact the accident has taken place in between 2 two wheeler vehicles.

Likewise, the R.W.2 has deposed in his evidence that, the complaint is lodged after delay of 5 days,
which clearly goes to show that, the insured vehicle has been falsely implicated.
Immediately after accident the petitioner was admitted to G. Modegowda Super Specialty Hospital.

The MLC Register Extract and Police Intimation of the said hospital discloses that, the accident has taken place between two wheeler and four wheeler vehicles and the same is over written as two wheeler.
14. No doubt, as rightly contended by the respondent No.2, there is over writing in the Ex.R.1 MLC Register Extract.
In place of the word 'Four wheeler' it has been overwritten as 'Two wheeler'.
Likewise, in the Ex.R.2 MLC intimation letter, sent to the jurisdictional Police Station, it is mentioned that, "A/H/O RTA in between two wheeler and four wheeler at 3:30 p.m."

But it is pertinent to note that, Dr. Mourya, Orthopedic Surgeon, who was the Casualty Medical Officer of G.
Madegowda Super Specialty Hospital, at the time when the petitioner was brought to the hospital,
has made endorsement in Ex.R.1 MLC Register Extract and Ex.R.2 MLC intimation letter, stating that, "the information given by patient attender by name Jayarama on 17-07-2022 at 04:42 p.m.,
was incorrect information of the accident.

He has conveyed earlier that, alleged road traffic accident took place between two wheeler and four wheeler, but actual the said accident has taken place between two wheeler and two wheeler which is informed and declared by the patient attender by name S.C. Kempaiyya on 17-07-2022 at 10:45 p.m., in the form of written letter".

Further it is endorsed that, they are hereby acknowledging the same and they want to reconfirm that, "the patient Kalappa, 42 years, male, brought to hospital with alleged history of road traffic accident between two wheeler and two wheeler at 03:30 p.m., near Sagaya on 17-07-2022".

Further, the said Dr. Mourya, who has been summoned and examined by the respondent No.2 as R.W.1, has clearly deposed in his cross- examination that, he has personal knowledge about Ex.R.1 & Ex.R.2 and the contents of said documents are true and correct.
Further he has clearly deposed that, as per initial statement given by the attendant of the patient the accident has taken place in between two wheeler and a four wheeler vehicles.
Later on the attendants again approached the duty doctor and stated that, the accident has taken place in between 2 two wheeler vehicles.
Infact the accident has taken place in between 2 two wheeler vehicles.

It is pertinent to note that, the above noted correction and endorsement in the MLC register and MLC intimation letter is made immediately on the very same day i.e. 17-07-2022 at 10:50 p.m., which is much prior to the date of lodging the complaint.

5 15.

Further it is pertinent to note that, as per Ex.P.4 Motor Vehicles Accident Report, the front right side head light mask and front mudguard of Yamaha motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-05-KG-8297 are damaged.
It is not the case of the respondents that, the said damage were already existing before the alleged date and time of the accident or the same have been caused in any other accident.

If really the said motorcycle was not at all involved in the accident in question, then the burden was on the respondents to explain, when, where and under what circumstances the above noted damage have been caused to the said vehicle, which the respondents have failed to discharge in the present case.
Therefore, in such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can safely be held that, the respondents have failed to establish the above contentions taken in their written statement.

Further, if really the accident had taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the petitioner/rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-11- EM-2089 himself and the offending Yamaha motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-05-KG-8297 was not at all involved in the said accident, the same could have been easily established by the respondents by examining the eye- witness to the alleged accident.
But, the respondents have not taken any strain to examine the eye-witness to the alleged accident, for the reasons best known to them.
Therefore, in such circumstances, there is absolutely no evidence on record to show that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the petitioner himself.

On the other hand, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending Yamaha motorcycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-05-KG-8297 and dashing the same to an ongoing motorcycle of the petitioner.

Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross-examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence or which goes to show that, the said accident has taken place solely due to his own rash and negligent riding or there was any contributory negligence on his part, in the cause of accident.

16. Further, the Ex.P.3 spot mahazer also clearly speaks that, the said accident has taken place on the left side of 16 feet wide on Halaguru-Rudrakshipura road, near Iggaluru Canal, Sagya Village,
Halaguru Hobli, Malavalli Taluk, Mandya District, in between offending Yamaha motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-05-KG-8297 and ongoing motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-11-EM-2089 of the petitioner.
Further, as per the Motor Vehicle Accident Report, which is marked as Ex.P.4, the accident has not taken place due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident.

When the accident was not caused due to the any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident and there was no negligence on the part of the petitioner/rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-11- EM-2089, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending vehicle.

Further, the investigation officer in his Ex.P.6 final report/charge-sheet has clearly stated that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending Yamaha motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-05-KG-8297 and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.

Admittedly, the said final report/charge-sheet has not been challenged either by the rider or the owner of offending vehicle bearing Reg.
No.KA-05-KG-8297.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident,
involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident, negligence of the rider of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.

6 17.
No doubt, there is a delay of five days in lodging the complaint by the petitioner.
But, the petitioner/complainant has stated the reason for delay in lodging the complaint in his Ex.P.2 first information statement.
He has clearly stated that, as he was undergoing treatment, there is delay caused in lodging the complaint.
It is settled proposition of law that, the delay in lodging FIR cannot be a ground to doubt claimant's case in genuine cases.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Ravi V/s Badrinarayan and others, reported in (2011)4 SCC 693, has clearly held that, "the delay in lodging FIR cannot be a ground to doubt claimant's case in genuine cases.

entities.text: Ravi V/s Badrinarayan and others, reported in (2011)4 SCC 693
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In Indian conditions, it is not expected that a person would to rush to police station after accident.
The treatment of victim is given priority over lodging FIR.
The kith and kin of victim are not expected to act mechanically with promptitude in lodging FIR.
Hence, delay in lodging FIR not a ground to dismiss claim petition."
18. There is absolutely no rebuttal or contrary evidence on record to disbelieve the reason for delay in lodging the complaint, stated in the Ex.P.2 first information statement.

In such circumstances and in the light of ratio laid down in the above cited decision, this Court is of the opinion that, in the present facts and circumstances of the case, the delay for lodging the complaint is properly explained by the petitioner with cogent and satisfactory reasons.

19. Further, on meticulously going through the Ex.P.5 wound certificate and Ex.P.8 discharge summary, it clearly reveals that, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in a road traffic accident i.e. head injury (subgaleal scalp haematoa), dental injury/fracture tooth.
There is absolutely no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondents to show that, the documents produced by the petitioner are false documents.

In such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can safely be held that, the respondents have failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner, regarding the rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-05-KG-8297 and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.

20. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
11 SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, " in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied."

22. Therefore, in the light of ratio laid down in the above cited decisions and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, he has sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident, occurred on 17-07-2022 at about 3.30 p.m., on Halaguru-Rudrakshipura road, near Iggaluru Canal, Sagya Village, Halaguru Hobli,
Malavalli Taluk, Mandya District, due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending Yamaha Kalappa.K vs Sudha.V on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/21673244/
7 motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-05-KG-8297.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Affirmative.
23. Issue No.2:

While answering above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, the accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending Yamaha motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-05-KG-8297 and he has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.

As per the medical records placed on record by the petitioner,
he has sustained head injury (subgaleal scalp haematoa), dental injury/fracture tooth.

Therefore,
this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.

The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants, transport, actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life,
loss of prospects of marriage etc.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
i) Towards loss of future income:
The petitioner has deposed that, earlier to the accident, he was working as Supervisor in Garments Company and earning a sum of Rs.25,000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his learning capacity.
But, the petitioner has neither produced any document nor examined any doctor to establish that, due to above injuries sustained in the accident he has suffered any physical disability or deformity.

The petitioner has failed to prove that, due to accidental injuries he has suffered any physical disability and he is not in a position to continue his avocation or perform his regular work and thereby, he has lost his learning capacity.
Further, it is pertinent to note that, the petitioner has clearly admitted in his cross-examination that, at present he is working at different place and getting salary of Rs.25,000/- per month.
This clearly goes to show that, due to injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner has not suffered any loss of future income.
In such circumstances, the question of awarding compensation under head loss of future income due to permanent physical disability does not arise at all.

Hence,
the petitioner is not entitled for any compensation under the head of loss of future income due to disability.
ii) Medical expenses:

The petitioner has deposed that, he has incurred expenses of Rs.1,00,000/-
towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charge etc.
In order to prove the same, he has produced 9 medical bills, as per Ex.P.9.
All the bills have been examined carefully and found that the petitioner has spent total amount of Rs.21,898/- towards medical expenses.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.21,898/- under the head of medical expenses.
iii) Pain and sufferings:
In the present case the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries i.e. head injury (subgaleal scalp haematoa), dental injury/fracture tooth.

As per Ex.P.8 discharge summary,
the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 2 days from 17-07-2022 to 18-07- 2022, in G.
Madegowda Super Speciality Hospital, Bharathinagara.

Therefore, taking into considering the injuries sustained by the petitioner, this Court is of the opinion that, compensation amount of Rs.30,000/-

vi) Conveyance expenses:

The petitioner is the resident of Kamalanagar, Shaneswara Temple,
Basaveshwaranagar, Bengaluru, the accident has occurred on Halaguru-Rudrakshipura road, near Iggaluru Canal, Sagya Village, Halaguru Hobli, Malavalli Taluk, Mandya District and he has taken treatment at G. Madegowda Super Speciality Hospital, Bharathinagara.

vii) Loss of income during treatment period:
The petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, before accident he was working as Supervisor in Garments Company and was earning a sum of Rs.25,000/- per month.
Further, he has deposed that, due to grievous injuries suffered in the said accident he is unable to do work and continue his avocation.
The respondent No.2 has specifically denied the same.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove his avocation and income.
But, the petitioner has failed to establish the same through cogent and corroborative evidence.
He has not produced any document to show that, before accident he was working as Supervisor in Garments Company and was earning a sum of Rs.25,000/- per month.
In such circumstances, there is no other option before this Court except to consider the notional income as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The accident has taken place in the year 2022.
Hence, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.15,500/- per month.
The petitioner has taken treatment for 2 days as in-patient at G. Madegowda Super Speciality Hospital, Bharathinagara, for the grievous injuries caused to him.

viii) Loss of amenities:

It is evident from the documents placed on record that, as on the date of accident the age of the petitioner was 48 years and unfortunately he has suffered grievous injuries in the said accident and undergone treatment for 2 days as in-patient in G. Madegowda Super Speciality Hospital, Bharathinagara.

24. Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads as follows:
1. Loss of future income -Nil- 2.
Medical expenses 21,898-00 3.
Pain and sufferings 30,000-00 4.
Attendant charges 2,000-00 5.
Food and nourishment 1,600-00 6.
Conveyance expenses 5,000-00 7. Loss of income during 15,500-00 treatment period 8. Loss of amenities 20,000-00
9. Future medical expenses -Nil-

In all, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.95,998/-
with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
25. Liability:
Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle bearing No.KA-05-KG-8297.

As per Ex.R.4 insurance policy, the policy issued by the respondent No.2 bearing No.3005/237258951/02/000, in respect of offending Yamaha motorcycle bearing No.KA-05- KG-8297 in favour of respondent No.1 was valid from 19-01- 2024 to 18-01-2025 and earlier policy was valid from 19-01- 2023 to 18-01-2024.

The R.W.2 has clearly admitted in her cross-examination that, as on the date of accident the insurance policy issued by their company in respect of the motorcycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-05-KG-8297 was valid.
Further, there is no evidence on record to show that, there is any breach of terms and conditions of said policy.

The evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No. KA-05-KG-8297 the said accident has occurred.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.1 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damage caused by the said vehicle.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.1.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.2 to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

Therefore, for the above stated reasons, holding that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.95,998/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization, from the respondent No.2, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.

opennyai_summary.facts: This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.
opennyai_summary.issue:
6. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.
Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident alleged to have occurred on 17-07-2022 at about 3.30 p.m., on Halaguru-Rudrakshipura road, near Iggaluru Canal, Sagya Village, Halaguru Hobli,
Malavalli Taluk, Mandya District, due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the Yamaha motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-05-KG-8297 ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation ?
If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3.
What order or Award ?
7.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It is not the case of the respondents that, the said damage were already existing before the alleged date and time of the accident or the same have been caused in any other accident.
If really the said motorcycle was not at all involved in the accident in question, then the burden was on the respondents to explain, when, where and under what circumstances the above noted damage have been caused to the said vehicle, which the respondents have failed to discharge in the present case.
Further, if really the accident had taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the petitioner/rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-11- EM-2089 himself and the offending Yamaha motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-05-KG-8297 was not at all involved in the said accident, the same could have been easily established by the respondents by examining the eye- witness to the alleged accident.
But, the respondents have not taken any strain to examine the eye-witness to the alleged accident, for the reasons best known to them.
Therefore, in such circumstances, there is absolutely no evidence on record to show that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the petitioner himself.
Admittedly, the said final report/charge-sheet has not been challenged either by the rider or the owner of offending vehicle bearing Reg.
No.KA-05-KG-8297.
In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident,
involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident, negligence of the rider of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.
No doubt, there is a delay of five days in lodging the complaint by the petitioner.
But, the petitioner/complainant has stated the reason for delay in lodging the complaint in his Ex.P.2 first information statement.
He has clearly stated that, as he was undergoing treatment, there is delay caused in lodging the complaint.
It is settled proposition of law that, the delay in lodging FIR cannot be a ground to doubt claimant's case in genuine cases.
18. There is absolutely no rebuttal or contrary evidence on record to disbelieve the reason for delay in lodging the complaint, stated in the Ex.P.2 first information statement.
In such circumstances and in the light of ratio laid down in the above cited decision, this Court is of the opinion that, in the present facts and circumstances of the case, the delay for lodging the complaint is properly explained by the petitioner with cogent and satisfactory reasons.
19. Further, on meticulously going through the Ex.P.5 wound certificate and Ex.P.8 discharge summary, it clearly reveals that, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in a road traffic accident i.e. head injury (subgaleal scalp haematoa), dental injury/fracture tooth.
There is absolutely no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondents to show that, the documents produced by the petitioner are false documents.
In such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can safely be held that, the respondents have failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner, regarding the rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-05-KG-8297 and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.
20. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.
But, the petitioner has neither produced any document nor examined any doctor to establish that, due to above injuries sustained in the accident he has suffered any physical disability or deformity.
The petitioner has failed to prove that, due to accidental injuries he has suffered any physical disability and he is not in a position to continue his avocation or perform his regular work and thereby, he has lost his learning capacity.
In such circumstances, the question of awarding compensation under head loss of future income due to permanent physical disability does not arise at all.
Hence,
the petitioner is not entitled for any compensation under the head of loss of future income due to disability.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove his avocation and income.
But, the petitioner has failed to establish the same through cogent and corroborative evidence.
He has not produced any document to show that, before accident he was working as Supervisor in Garments Company and was earning a sum of Rs.25,000/- per month.
The accident has taken place in the year 2022.
Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, awarding compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards loss of amenities during the treatment period would be just and reasonable.
In such circumstances, the question of awarding compensation for future medical expenses does not arise at all.
Further, there is no evidence on record to show that, there is any breach of terms and conditions of said policy.
The evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No. KA-05-KG-8297 the said accident has occurred.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.1 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damage caused by the said vehicle.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.1.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.2 to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
